mental_model: It fuses back-to-back vector-function calls in the root kernel into one merged vector function, so the vector cores pay the per-call scheduling cost once instead of once per fragment. Whether a pair may fuse is proven by dependency and memory-effect analysis, and the pass runs in one of two mutually exclusive placements: before bufferization on tensor IR, or after it on memref IR.
need: A kernel outlined into many small vector-function (VF) callees pays per-VF call and scheduling overhead on the vector cores, which dominates execution time for small kernels; the knowledge memory records this intent verbatim.
responsibility: Collect the module's VFs, order them by root call order, prove which adjacent call pairs are compatible, and rewrite the call graph so safe adjacent pairs become one merged VF function behind a single call.
observable_outcome: A module with fewer VF functions and fewer VF calls: e.g. two tensor-level attention VFs become one merged VF returning 4 results (L1 fixture), or two memref-level rms-norm VFs become one merged VF with an 11-argument signature (L2 fixture).

audience_contract.who: compiler/runtime engineers familiar with MLIR passes and bufferization, who have never read MergeVecScope.cpp
audience_contract.assumed_knowledge: MLIR pass pipeline basics, func/memref/tensor dialects, what bufferization is
audience_contract.not_assumed: this pass's internals, HFusion VF outlining details, the A5 codebase

triggers.interaction: adds the pass once — with mergeLevel=1 pre-bufferization, or mergeLevel=2 post-bufferization; 0 or unset means the pass never runs

upstream.interaction: produces the module shape this pass requires: one non-VF root function plus hivm.vector_function-marked callees reached by func.call
runs before the level-2 placement, so L2 sees memref IR instead of tensor IR

downstream.entity: bufferization (L1 path) and later convert-to-hivm lowering
downstream.interaction: consume the merged call graph; the merged bodies are lowered like any other VF

inputs.name: module with root + VF callees
inputs.form: ModuleOp: exactly one non-VF func (root) plus funcs marked hivm.vector_function called via func.call
inputs.description: the pass returns early if no root exists

inputs.name: pass options
inputs.description: level selects strategy, limit caps how many original VFs one merged VF may contain

outputs.name: rewritten module
outputs.form: merged func.func marked hivm.vector_function + one fused func.call per merge (attrs ptc_simdvf, no_inline preserved/copied)
outputs.description: original VFs and their calls erased; gap ops either moved aside or lifted into the merged body

mechanism.summary: Seven source-derived stages: collect VFs and sort them into root call order; build same-block dependency facts (SSA + memref alias) and close them transitively; score forward usage and order dependency-free VFs first; greedily try to fuse call-adjacent pairs under the level and count limits; prove each pair legal through a gate cascade; rewrite via one of two merge shapes; maintain the dependency bookkeeping and self-verify the merged function.

stages.name: Collect & order
stages.what: walk module for hivm::isVF funcs; find the single non-VF root; reorder vfs by first-call order in the root, appending never-called VFs

stages.name: Build dependency facts
stages.what: union memref alias sets over the root; record same-block SSA deps and same-block memref Read/Write deps (dominance-filtered); compute the transitive dependency closure used by every later decision

stages.name: Score & prioritize
stages.what: fill a forward-usage score matrix (i feeds j) from call-pair dependencies; stable_partition puts zero-score (dependency-free) VFs first; build the VFDependencyGraph with reverse edges

stages.name: Greedy merge loop
stages.what: take call-adjacent pairs from the ordered vfs; level 1 requires the pair be unrelated in the VF graph; the merged-VF count limit caps fusions; on success the merged VF replaces the pair in the list and is re-queued so chains can fuse further

stages.name: Prove pair legality
stages.what: gate cascade: compatible result extract kinds; same parent region; no SyncBlockSet/SyncBlockWait in the gap; anchor-bearing ops are pinned and must not feed call2; gap memory ops must be movable (after vf2, before vf1, or splittable); level 1 additionally requires an empty residual gap

stages.name: Rewrite
stages.what: move the movable gap ops out of the way; then either mergeNoBetween (empty gap: fuse calls, dedup vf2 args fed by vf1 results, clone both bodies, concat returns) or mergeNoMemory (lift gap mem ops into the merged body; used-after intermediates become extra results/args); patch calls and erase originals

stages.name: Maintain & verify
stages.what: update allDepsClosure and VFDependencyGraph for every merge (merged node inherits both neighbors); erase old VFs after the loop; mergedFunc.verify() failure signals pass failure

control_flow: pipeline (HIVMRegbasePipelines) drives the pass once, gated by enableVfMergeLevel
runOnOperation drives collect → facts → score → greedy loop; tryMerge drives the gate cascade and dispatches to exactly one of mergeNoBetween / mergeNoMemory
nothing else mutates the module: the pass is the sole rewriter in its scope
data_flow: alias facts: root ops → MemrefAliasAnalysisState unions → isAlias predicates inside analyzeMemrefDepdencies
dependency facts: op-level SSA/memref deps → combinedDeps → allDepsClosure (transitive) → isDep queries in scoring and gap moving
IR: gap memory ops flow out of the call gap (moved aside) or into the merged function body (mergeNoMemory); call2 args fed by call1 results are redirected to vf1's cloned results
VF list: vfs starts as all VFs and monotonically shrinks as pairs fuse; merged VFs re-enter the loop

implementation_view.description: vfs (ordered VF list), allDepsClosure (transitive op dependency map), useScoreMat/useScoreTotal (forward usage), numVFInMergedVF (fusion count accounting), VFDependencyGraph (forward+reverse adjacency with mergeNodes/verify)

mergeNoBetween handles the empty-gap case with pure call fusion; mergeNoMemory additionally clones gap memory ops into the merged function and widens its signature — chosen by whether the gap is empty after moving
ops containing hir.anchor IDs and their SSA neighbors are closed over and pinned; pinned ops stay in place and their results must not feed call2, or the merge is rejected

one O(n^2) same-block memref dependency scan over all root ops; dependency closure computed once and incrementally patched on merge; LLVM_DEBUG logging throughout (score matrix, VF graph, before/after counts)

conceptual_view.description: the only thing being optimized is per-VF call/scheduling overhead; merging N VFs pays the cost once, at the price of a wider call signature when intermediates must survive

every fusion is gated on dependency/memory evidence, not heuristics about profitability — the pass declines (skips) rather than guesses; the two riskiest rewrites (sync-crossing, anchor reorder) are hard-rejected

the level option is really a placement choice: fuse early on tensor IR (level 1, dependency-free pairs only) or late on memref IR (level 2, any pair within the count limit); both share the same rewrite machinery
the pass verifies each merged function it builds and signals pass failure on invalid output — an unusually strong self-check for a rewrite pass

canonical_example.initial_state: root @_attn_fwd_scope_0_outlined calls two adjacent VFs @_attn_fwd_scope_0_outlined_manual_vf_0 and ..._vf_1 (tensor<64x64xf32> tiles); vfs = [vf_0, vf_1] in call order

Score: no forward usage between the two VFs → both dependency-free (startVFs)
Greedy loop: pair (vf_0, vf_1) adjacent, unrelated (level 1), 1+1 ≤ 4 → tryMerge
Legality: extract kinds compatible, same region, no sync ops in gap, nothing pinned, gap empty after checks → mergeNoBetween
Rewrite: merged func cloned vf_0 body then vf_1 body; one fused call replaces both; results concatenated
important_states: call list: two calls → one 4-result call (ptc_simdvf set)

state_transitions.reason: greedy fusion must respect program order

state_transitions.operation: tryMerge → mergeNoBetween → patchCalls; erase old VFs
state_transitions.after: call merged_vf_0 with 4 results (ptc_simdvf); vfs shrinks by one

state_transitions.after: one call to merged__merged_vf_0 with 11 args / 4 results

decisions.question: Which VF pairs are candidates at all?
decisions.condition: mergeLevel option (0 / 1 / 2) plus position in call-ordered vfs
outcomes: 1 → only adjacent pairs unrelated in the VF dependency graph
2 → any adjacent pair, subject to the count limit
decisions.reason: the option is the user-facing strategy selector, mirrored by two mutually exclusive pipeline gates

decisions.question: May the code between the two calls be disturbed?
decisions.condition: gap contents: sync ops present? anchor-bearing ops and their SSA neighbors? do memory ops depend on call1 / feed call2?
outcomes: sync op in gap → reject merge
pinned (anchor) ops must not feed call2 → reject if they do
all gap mem ops movable after vf2 → move them there
…or all movable before vf1 → move them there
…or SplitMove succeeds → split around the VFs
level 1 with any residual unpinned gap → reject
decisions.reason: the gap is shared state between two rewrites; correctness comes from refusing to reorder what must not move

decisions.question: Which merge shape applies?
outcomes: empty → mergeNoBetween: pure call fusion, vf2 args fed by vf1 results are deduplicated
non-empty → mergeNoMemory: gap mem ops are cloned into the merged body; used-after intermediates widen the merged signature
decisions.reason: an empty gap needs no body merging beyond concatenation; a non-empty gap must be absorbed somewhere — the merged function is the only safe home

decisions.question: Are the two VFs' results compatible?
decisions.condition: hasCompatibleResultExtractKind: both all-extract or both non-extract
outcomes: mismatched → reject (extracted result would convert V->S wait and prevent double buffering)
decisions.reason: result consumption shape is a hardware-buffering constraint, not a data dependency

strategies.name: L1 — merge at tensor level, pre-bufferization
strategies.mechanism: runs before tensor-copy-insertion/OneShotBufferize; merges only dependency-free adjacent pairs; empty residual gap required
strategies.cost: conservative coverage (skips related pairs); no memref alias facts available yet

strategies.name: L2 — merge at memref level, post-bufferization
strategies.mechanism: runs immediately after OneShotBufferize; merges any adjacent pair within mergeVFNumLimit, trusting the dependency closure to gate safety
strategies.cost: wider coverage; operates on concrete memref IR with buffer-level alias facts

dimensions.preconditions: dependency-free adjacent pairs only | any adjacent pair within mergeVFNumLimit
dimensions.ir_form: tensor IR (vector ops on tensors) | memref IR (loads/stores/allocs)
dimensions.mechanism: same gate cascade; level-1 additionally demands an empty residual gap | same machinery; gap mem ops lifted into merged body (mergeNoMemory path)
dimensions.observed_output: merged call returns 4 tensor results (attention fixture) | merged VF has 11 memref args / 4 results (rms-norm fixture)
dimensions.rationale: bufferization sees the smaller call graph | concrete alias facts replace the conservative same-block-only analysis
dimensions.risk: declines legal merges (cross-block deps invisible) | merged bodies carry bufferization-side memory effects

contracts.element: module shape: one non-VF root func + hivm.vector_function-marked callees invoked by func.call
merged VF functions (hivm.vector_function) and fused calls carrying ptc_simdvf (+ preserved call attrs)
merge-level / merge-vf-num-limit options; enableVfMergeLevel pipeline gate (0 disables entirely)

constraints.statement: the two calls must share one parent region (no merging across scf.if/scf.for bodies)
no SyncBlockSet/SyncBlockWait op may sit in the merge gap
anchor-bearing ops (hir.anchor IDs) and their SSA neighbors stay pinned; a pinned result feeding call2 rejects the merge
result extract kinds must match (all-extract or all-non-extract) to preserve double buffering
merged function must self-verify; failure signals pass failure
func core types of the two VFs must match

invariants.statement: vfs list stays in root call order; fusion only replaces an adjacent pair with a merged VF at the same position
VFDependencyGraph forward and reverse edges stay consistent (verify asserts after every mutation)

assumptions.statement: each VF is called at most once ('Assume each vf is used only once...' — MergeVecScope.cpp:631); multi-use VFs would make the dependency reasoning wrong
same-block dependency scanning is sufficient for the merges attempted today (cross-block deps are invisible)

boundaries.statement: fusing adjacent, same-region VF pairs with compatible extract kinds: dependency-free pairs at L1, any pairs within the count limit at L2
cross-block memory dependencies are invisible to the analysis (same-block scans), so some legal cross-block merges on attention-shaped roots are declined — recorded as MVS-002
merges crossing sync_block set/wait ops, or that would reorder anchor IDs, or with mismatched extract kinds
merge-level=0 disables the pass entirely (pipeline gate or option)
a VF called from more than one call site violates the single-use assumption; no guard checks call-site counts — recorded as open finding MVS-001
behavior when the count-limit check interacts with re-queued merged VFs beyond the fixtures' two-VF shapes (no test covers >2 chained fusions in the reviewed corpus)

placement.why_here: the pass needs a whole-module view of the root's VF call graph plus dominance and alias analyses, and its placement is itself the strategy selector: level 1 sits before tensor-copy-insertion/OneShotBufferize so bufferization plans around the merged call graph, level 2 sits immediately after OneShotBufferize so merges see concrete memref alias facts
placement.why_not_earlier: before VF outlining there are no vector functions to merge; before the call order exists in the root, adjacency — the pass's core candidate criterion — is undefined
placement.why_not_later: at level 1, merging after bufferization would forfeit the tensor-level benefit (bufferization plans one merged body instead of two); at level 2, waiting beyond bufferization would lose the memref alias facts that justify the wider coverage

key_takeaways: It amortizes vector-core call/scheduling overhead by fusing call-adjacent VF pairs into one merged vector function.
Safety is proven, not guessed: a gate cascade (extract kinds, region, sync ops, anchor pinning, gap movability) precedes every rewrite, and each merged function is self-verified.

The level option is really two strategies in one pass: L1 fuses tensor-level VFs before bufferization (dependency-free pairs only), L2 fuses memref-level VFs after it (wider coverage, concrete alias facts).
Gap handling is the hard part: sync ops and anchor-pinned ops are hard rejections; movable memory ops are either moved aside or absorbed into the merged body (widening its signature).
Known edges: the single-call-per-VF assumption is unguarded (MVS-001), and the same-block-only dependency scan declines some legal cross-block merges (MVS-002).
design_tradeoffs: Greedy adjacent-pair fusion preserves program order but cannot fuse non-adjacent VFs even when provably independent (EV-021).
Self-verification (mergedFunc.verify → signalPassFailure) trades compile-time robustness for a hard failure instead of silently emitting broken IR (EV-011).
mergeNoMemory widens call signatures to keep used-after intermediates alive — fewer calls at the price of fatter call boundaries (EV-023).
risks: MVS-001 (open, correctness): multi-call-site VF merged on wrong dependency data — medium regression risk per the knowledge memory.
MVS-002 (open, opportunity): cross-block merges declined on attention-shaped roots.

pass.operation_scope: module-wide VF call graph rooted at the single non-VF function

ir_contract.before: L1: tensor-form VF calls (vector ops on tensor<...>); L2: memref-form VF calls (loads/stores on memref<...>)
ir_contract.after: one merged func.func (hivm.vector_function) per fusion whose body is the cloned concatenation of both bodies (plus lifted gap mem ops in mergeNoMemory), driven by one fused call with concatenated results and attrs ptc_simdvf / no_inline

attributes.creator: sets ptc_simdvf unit attr on every fused call; marks merged funcs with hivm.vector_function; preserves other call attrs (callee/result_segment_sizes excluded)
attributes.consumer: downstream VF lowering and double-buffering logic consume ptc_simdvf and the vector_function marker

pass.legality: see decisions D1–D4 and constraints: region identity, sync/anchor exclusions, extract-kind compatibility, gap movability, count limit, core-type match
pass.rewrite: mergeNoBetween (empty gap: call fusion + arg dedup) and mergeNoMemory (non-empty gap: gap mem ops lifted, used-after intermediates become extra results); both patch calls, RAUW results, erase originals
